text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1952103456 - Cross-region routing anomalies detected. Automatic failover from eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 triggered for some customer traffic. Pager fired. Bridge: https://zoom.redwood/incident/1952103456. Severity: Sev2. Initial metric: 5xx rate spike in eu-west-1 up to 18% at 2026-03-15T02:24Z.

Alice M: acked, I'm watching service-level dashboards now. Seeing elevated 502/504 on /v1/generate for hosted.api.eu-west-1. Not all hosts are affected; seems tied to a subset of AZ B instances.

Dan L: oncall (sre) here, joining the bridge. Any immediate customer-facing blocker?

Alice M: customer reports: two PLG customers saw timeouts and a few pay-as-you-go calls returned 502. Dedicated customers on eu-west-1 reported degraded throughput but not full outage.

Bob S: Network: I'm seeing partial BGP withdraws in eu-west-1-A and a flurry of DNS NXDOMAINs for our internal edge domains from that AZ. Might be an inter-AZ fabric issue at the provider. Correlates with route flaps at 02:21Z.

Carla R: Confirmed. Healthchecks are failing for internal NLBs in that AZ. The autoscaler started draining a few nodes, but the draining didn't finish for some pods because connections are stuck in CLOSE_WAIT. Could explain 'unhealthy failover' behavior where traffic shifts but some backends still accept ephemeral connections.

Dan L: taking lead on mitigation. Short plan: 1) Quarantine problematic AZ by marking hosts unhealthy in service registry. 2) Force Route53 weighted routing to prefer us-east-1 for affected endpoints. 3) If necessary, scale up us-east-1 pools and apply cache-warm policy.

Eve K: oncall warming up. I'll prepare the Route53 change and pre-scale us-east-1 workers.

Dan L: doing the quarantine now. Running the drain/mark-unhealthy script:

```
# Mark eu-west-1-A nodes as unhealthy in consul
./ops/mark-hosts-unhealthy --region eu-west-1 --az eu-west-1-a --tag edge
# quick check
consul members | grep eu-west-1-a
```

Dan L: output showed about 8 hosts in eu-west-1-a flagged; starting deregistration.

Eve K: pushing Route53 weight change to shift 80% -> us-east-1 for api.redwood.internal. Command:

```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.internal","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1","Weight":20,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.10.10.10"}]}},{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.internal","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-east-1","Weight":80,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.20.20.20"}]}}]}'
```

Eve K: Route53 change propagated (console shows pending, TTL 30s). Pre-scaling us-east-1 +30% workers now:

```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-workers --replicas=260 --context us-east-1
```

Alice M: after weight change, 5xxs dropped to ~3% in 2m, but some long-tail user requests still hit eu-west-1 and fail. The bridge shows sticky connections to old load balancers.

Bob S: provider confirmed an AZ-level networking flap persisted ~10 minutes causing some control-plane packets to be lost. Their remediation started at 02:34Z. They expect BGP sessions to stabilize in ~15 min.

Dan L: because draining wasn't completing, I'm running a more aggressive connection flush on NLBs in eu-west-1-A. Command:

```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10
```

Dan L: after setting deregistration delay to 10s and forcibly closing stuck connections, pods finished shutdown. Healthchecks returning to healthy for other AZs.

Eve K: confirming traffic now ~95% in us-east-1. Latency bump of ~40ms for EU-origin traffic but overall error rate acceptable. Customer-facing status page updated: https://status.redwood/incident/1952103456.

Alice M: Customer-impact summary for status page draft: 'We observed elevated errors and timeouts from eu-west-1 between 02:21Z - 02:40Z due to an AZ-level networking issue at cloud provider. Automatic failover redirected traffic to us-east-1; most customers saw degraded latency; a small percentage experienced 5xx errors. We're monitoring and working with provider.' Approve?

Frank T: approved. Suggest adding affected customer list (internal ticket IDs) and noting which Dedicated customers had degraded throughput. I'll open the follow-up ticket.

Dan L: handing off primary incident lead to Eve K (next shift). Handoff summary: cause = provider AZ network flap -> route flaps + DNS anomalies. Immediate mitigation = quarantine AZ, Route53 weighted shift to us-east-1, forced deregistration/delayed dereg timeout change, pre-scale us-east-1. Current state = traffic shifted, error rate back to baseline (~1%), provider working on full network restoration.

Eve K: taking over. I'll keep monitoring for 1 hour and coordinate with provider for RCA. Will create postmortem doc and link here.

Carla R: action item: investigate why draining left connections in CLOSE_WAIT. Possibly kernel-level TIME_WAIT handling and our connection pool timeouts. I'll open task INFRA-6227.

Frank T: customer communications note: prepare targeted messages to 3 highest-usage customers (they saw >10% error rates). Use this template: "We're sorry — between 02:21Z and 02:40Z your requests routed through eu-west-1 experienced elevated errors due to a provider-level network issue. We've rerouted traffic and applied mitigations; please reach out if you saw persistent errors."

Dan L: logging final mitigation timestamps in incident tracker. Marking first mitigation at 2026-03-15T02:26Z (Route53 change), AZ quarantine at 02:27Z, forced dereg at 02:30Z.

incident-bot: Incident updated (status: mitigating -> monitoring). Bridge remains open for 60m.

Eve K: postmortem TODOs I'll manage: 1) provider RCA follow-up 2) improve draining script + healthcheck hysteresis 3) automate emergency route53 weight rollbacks 4) add synthetic end-to-end tests for failover behavior (INFRA-6228, INFRA-6229, INFRA-6230).

Frank T: nice containment and clear handoff. Please ensure we add a timeline and customer impact table in postmortem. I'll take ownership of customer comms drafts.

Alice M: closing loop: monitoring shows slow return of eu-west-1 capacity; provider says full stability at 02:46Z. I'll keep an eye for 30m then we can close the incident if metrics hold.

Eve K: will post the postmortem link here when created. Thanks all for fast reactions. :thumbsup:
